events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Arrested
events.description: Anne Boleyn, the second wife of Henry VIII, was arrested and taken to the Tower of London. She was accused of adultery and other charges that most historians regard as fabricated.
events.significance: Her arrest began a swift fall from power that ended in her execution later that month. It remains one of the best-known court scandals in English history.

events.title: Madrid Rises Against French Occupation
events.description: The people of Madrid rebelled against Napoleon's French forces occupying the city. French troops put down the uprising brutally. Goya later commemorated the day in his painting The Second of May 1808.
events.significance: The revolt set off the Peninsular War, a long struggle that drained Napoleonic France. The Spanish still mark the date as the Day of Madrid.

events.title: The Jet Age Takes Off
events.description: The De Havilland Comet 1 flew the world's first scheduled passenger jet service, carrying fare-paying travelers from London to Johannesburg.
events.significance: The Comet showed that jet travel was faster and smoother than propeller flight. It pointed the way to modern air travel.

events.title: The General Belgrano Is Sunk
events.description: During the Falklands War, the British submarine HMS Conqueror sank the Argentine cruiser ARA General Belgrano. The attack killed 323 people.
events.significance: It was the deadliest single event of the Falklands War and caused more than half of Argentina's casualties in the conflict. The Argentine fleet stayed in port for the rest of the war, and the sinking remains controversial.

events.title: Osama bin Laden Is Killed
events.description: A U.S. special operations team killed al-Qaeda founder Osama bin Laden in a raid on his compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan. The date is May 2 in local time.
events.significance: The raid ended a decade-long manhunt for the man behind the September 11, 2001 attacks. It marked a major moment in the global fight against terrorism.
